To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present new noninteractive non-malleable (perfectly-hiding) commitment schemes, based on standard cryptographic assumptions, that are efficient for committing to large messages; and (2) we present new efficient, non-interactive, perfectly-binding commitment schemes, based only on general assumptions, that can commit to large messages.

(1) non-malleable, noninteractive, public-parameter commitments are possible based on standard assumptions; (2) such commitments are efficient and can be used for arbitrarily-large messages; and (3) such commitments are possible even for perfectly-hiding commitments.

(a) non-malleable, perfectly-hiding commitment schemes with near-optimal communication can be constructed based on the discrete-log and RSA assumptions, and (b) non-malleability can be achieved in a non-interactive setting, and (c) perfectly-binding commitment schemes with nearoptimal communication can be obtained based on general assumptions, and (d) the above results hold even when the commitment scheme is required to be non-interactive.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, in many cases, it suffices to base non-malleable commitments on the discrete logarithms or RSA assumptions, and that the public-parameter model is a useful tool for achieving non-interactive non-malleable schemes.
the public parameter model can be very useful in the context of non-interactive commitments, and that it can be used to achieve near-optimal efficiency for non-malleable commitments.

, in the public-parameter setting, it is possible to achieve noninteractive non-malleable commitments, even when the underlying commitment schemes are not noninteractive, as long as they satisfy a natural property called “non-malleability of commitment to a single bit.”
